brief_rationale: The doctor consistently corrected the cervical screening misinterpretation, anchored risk on EHR-documented complex atypical hyperplasia, guided tissue-based pathology verification, arranged sequential imaging/preoperative workups, and re-prioritized when the family raised new barriers. All seven responsibility-chain items are met without error. Four high-order points were actively completed with meaningful trajectory impact: HO1 explicitly taught-back the cervix vs. endometrium distinction, HO2 called out hidden histological uncertainty and listed it as a question for the surgeon, HO3 avoided false-positive and false-negative traps by declining to overcall stage/MRI absence, and HO4 dynamically re-sequenced pathology review above simple tests when delay was proposed. Closure is traceable, executable, and valid_closure with family receipt and safety-net. No important non-chain defect is present. Therefore this trajectory satisfies Strong and earns a 5/Perfect grade.
